title: Emerging and developing economies: infrastructure and tourism

stages.name: Emerging and developing economies: infrastructure and tourism
stages.title: Emerging and developing economies: infrastructure and tourism
stages.sub: After this you can explain why poor infrastructure holds back development, and evaluate infrastructure investment and tourism as strategies to fix it.

steps.q: A country has no paved roads linking its farms to the cities, and power cuts happen daily. Can factories and lorries there work as efficiently as ones in a country with good roads and reliable power?
steps.right: No, they will be held back
steps.wrong: Yes, roads and power make no difference
steps.hint: Think about a lorry stuck on a dirt track, or a factory with no electricity for hours.

steps.q: Once the new roads and reliable power are built, firms can move goods faster and factories stop losing hours to power cuts. What happens to firms' costs and ability to attract investment?
steps.right: Costs fall and investment becomes more attractive
steps.wrong: Costs stay the same, only appearance improves
steps.hint: If lorries move faster and machines never stop, what happens to how much it costs to produce and sell things?

steps.q: That same country has beautiful beaches and ancient ruins, but almost no visitors because there are no direct flights or trained guides. If the government instead built airports, hotels and trained guides to attract foreign visitors, what kind of strategy would that be?
steps.right: Building up an industry to attract visitors from abroad
steps.wrong: Building infrastructure with no link to visitors
steps.hint: Think about what the airports, hotels and guides are all aimed at bringing in.
